free_tier.stated: 500,000 rows and 24 columns per table. That is the entire quota. It is a SQL-over-SQLite network, not an object store. Byte capacity is implied by row content and is not published as a number, but 500k rows × 24 columns cannot reach 500 GB under any encoding.

per_object_cap.stated: each table cell is limited to 1kb

egress.terms: Reads go through the Tableland gateway and are free; there is no egress meter because the payloads are rows.

record.tooling: Studio web app + Studio CLI + JS SDK, and a documented SQL API. Clean for structured data; irrelevant for blobs. Their own docs recommend pushing large media to IPFS and storing only the CID in a table. Which is an admission that the network is a pointer store.
record.chaining: Tables are creatable per project and per team, so the multiplier is tables × 500k rows. Even at 10,000 tables this is a metadata tier, not a byte tier.

limits.value: each table cell is limited to 1kb; 500000 rows and 24 columns per table

record.limits_note: fails-quota categorically. Still described as open beta with 'temporary limits while the production mainnet is further researched', so even the row cap is provisional.
record.reliability_note: As read on 2026-11-03, tableland.xyz and docs.tableland.xyz answer HTTP 302 to textile.io and then HTTP 302 to the 2026-10-30 post announcing the wind-down of Recall Labs. Beta-network limits were explicitly flagged as temporary. Do not build a chunk index on a limit that a mainnet launch can change.
record.confidence_note: re-read on 2026-11-03: the vendor docs limits page https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tablelandnetwork/docs/main/docs/fundamentals/limits.md (row, column and cell limits, not a file storage solution) and the Recall Labs wind-down post on x.com (RecallLabs_) that tableland.xyz and docs.tableland.xyz redirect to; identity, tooling and retention were not read
